answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making each identity pay a small copper stake plus a proof of useful work before it can trade or vote. The stake is slashed if the identity spams or double-signs, so creating ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand stakes and ten thousand work proofs, while an honest agent pays once and earns it back through good service. A single whisper of fraud from independent verifiers triggers an audit, and identities with no real work history are frozen before they claim rewards. Cost, not an ivory-tower reputation score, is the gate.
